title: Two-Way Coupled Dynamics of Quantized Vortex Bundle Formation in Spatially Periodic Normal-Fluid Turbulence
authors: Hiromichi Kobayashi, Makoto Tsubota, Rio Yokota
abstract: Using fully coupled two-way simulations combining the vortex filament model with the Navier--Stokes equations, we discover that quantized vortices in superfluid $^4$He are systematically rolled up into coherent bundles within normal-fluid vortex tubes. Although co-rotating quantized vortices do not aggregate spontaneously, mutual friction with the normal fluid actively drives their bundling, directly inheriting the spatial hierarchy of classical turbulence. Mutual friction excites high-wavenumber normal-fluid vortex tubes adjacent to quantized vortices, while the superfluid forms a nested structure of thick low-wavenumber outer tubes and fine high-wavenumber inner tubes around the vortex lines. A distinct time lag between superfluid kinetic energy and dissipation fuels the energy cascade, giving rise to Kolmogorov's $k^{-5/3}$ spectrum. Crucially, bundle lifetimes are governed by the ratio of the local coupling time scale $t_\mathrm{cl}$ to the Kolmogorov dissipation time scale $τ_η$ ($t_\mathrm{cl}/τ_η< 20$), leading to enhanced thermal stability at higher temperatures. These findings establish a unified mechanism for two-fluid multiscale vortex organization.
summary: This work simulates the coupled dynamics of superfluid and normal fluid in helium to understand quantized vortex bundling. The key finding is that mutual friction drives this bundling, creating a nested structure within normal-fluid tubes. This establishes a quantitative criterion for the stability of these quantum vortex bundles.
main_problem: The study investigates the mechanism by which quantized vortices in superfluid helium form coherent bundles within the surrounding normal-fluid vortex tubes.
main_result: Mutual friction with the normal fluid actively drives vortex bundling, leading to a nested superfluid structure and establishing a condition (t_cl/tau_eta < 20) for enhanced thermal stability.
method: The research employs fully coupled two-way simulations combining the Vortex Filament Model (VFM) for the superfluid and the Navier-Stokes equations for the normal fluid.
model_or_system: The system is superfluid Helium ($	ext{He}$) modeled as a two-fluid mixture, where dynamics are governed by the coupling force of mutual friction between the superfluid and normal fluid components.
key_observables: Energy spectra ($	ext{En}(k)$, $	ext{Es}(k)$), vortex line density, superfluid and normal fluid vorticities, and the ratio of local coupling time scale ($	ext{t}_{	ext{cl}}$) to Kolmogorov dissipation time scale ($	au_{\eta}$).
important_parameters: The ratio $	ext{t}_{	ext{cl}}/	au_{\eta}$ is crucial for determining bundle lifetime and thermal stability; the coupling strength is influenced by temperature.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes spatially periodic normal-fluid turbulence and utilizes the two-fluid model framework.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate instantaneous vortex distributions, time-averaged energy spectra showing $k^{-5/3}$ scaling, and time evolution plots tracking energy, vorticity, and the coupling time scale ratio.
paper_structure: The paper develops the coupled equations, simulates the dynamics, analyzes the energy spectra and vortex structures, and concludes by deriving the condition governing the stability and formation of vortex bundles.
why_interesting: The detailed study of energy cascade and multiscale organization in a quantum fluid system provides insights into non-equilibrium dynamics and energy transfer mechanisms relevant to quantum turbulence.
